result.title: Segment What It Can Draw: Querying a Text-to-Image Generator with Its Own Images for Skin Lesion Segmentation
result.summary: Skin lesion segmentation without annotated masks requires the target to be specified through other cues. Existing approaches rely on dermoscopy-specific rules, annotation-derived model priors, or user-selected regions. A general text-to-image diffusion transformer offers a text interface to the target, but its concept-word attention is unreliable on dermoscopy images: in the model's attention-output space, the word-derived skin-to-lesion direction is poorly aligned with the direction separating real skin from real lesions. We show that the direction derived from generated healthy-skin and lesion images is substantially better aligned. Based on this finding, we propose GENIQ, a training-free method that constructs initial skin and lesion prototypes from generated images and refines them using the most skin-like and lesion-like patches from unlabelled dermoscopy images. It scores test patches along the refined direction and applies a gated threshold to suppress contextual spill-over around small lesions. Without inference-time annotations or additional models, GENIQ achieves Dice scores of 0.85-0.88 on three dermoscopy test sets. It outperforms zero-shot and word-based attention methods on all three sets, and a hand-designed dermoscopy pipeline in Dice and IoU on two.

AI.brief_summary: 为免除皮肤病变分割对标注掩码的依赖，作者发现 T2I 扩散 Transformer 中由生成图像得到的「皮肤—病变」方向比概念词注意力方向更对齐，据此提出免训练方法 GENIQ：由生成图构造初始原型，用无标注皮肤镜图像中最像皮肤/病变的 patch 精炼，再沿该方向打分并用门控阈值抑制小病变周围溢出。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属分割应用而非推理，但其在扩散模型内部注意力—输出空间用合成数据构造方向原型、再以真实 patch 精炼并做门控筛选的做法，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、内部状态读出的具体线索相关，值得核查。
